headline: All four arms measured for the first time. At n=292 the arms are statistically indistinguishable — the curve is FLAT within noise, and no replay ratio can be derived from it.
what_unblocked_it: Every prior attempt died at quartet2/quant.py:120 `assert x.shape[0] % 128 == 0`, reached through model.generate(): with a KV cache each decode step feeds ONE row. eval_generative now routes Quartet models through score_sentinel_live._greedy_generate_quartet. Before this the curve read fit.status incomplete / n_points 0 with probe_eval null on all four arms.
verdict: MEASURED, FLAT, AND UNRESOLVABLE ON THIS DOMAIN. 0 of 6 pairwise comparisons are significant even under the optimistic independent-n assumption, and clustering lowers the z-scores further. Resolving a ~0.05 effect needs hundreds of additional DISTINCT FACTS, which Kanto does not have while its extraction gate is failing.
to_resolve: ~1373 forced-choice items per arm would be needed to resolve the largest observed gap (0.0514) at alpha 0.05 / power 0.80. Current n is 292 per arm.
controls_held: base_acc 0.2808 and n=292 identical across all four arms, so the deltas are comparable.
note_on_r010_exit_1: r010's driver exit=1 is a VERDICT, not a crash: its forced-choice axis PASSED and only the generative axis missed its bar. The eval ran to completion and wrote its report.

CORRECTION_clustering.what: The reported n=292 counts probe ITEMS, not independent observations. data/pokemon-lore/kanto/probes.jsonl holds 300 items over just 75 distinct source triples — exactly 4 surfaces each, across 35 subjects. A model either knows a fact or does not, so the 4 paraphrases of one fact are strongly correlated.
CORRECTION_clustering.consequence: Every interval built from n=292 as if independent is too narrow. Design effect is 1+(m-1)*rho with m=4, so n_eff = 292/DEFF: 154 at rho=0.3, 117 at 0.5, 94 at 0.7, and 73 (the fact count) at rho=1.
CORRECTION_clustering.does_not_change_the_verdict: The arms were already indistinguishable at the optimistic independent-n assumption (largest z=1.29). Correcting for clustering only lowers it further — z falls to 0.82 at rho=0.5 and 0.73 at rho=0.7. The curve is flat, more firmly than first reported.
CORRECTION_clustering.changes_the_prescription: My earlier 'needs ~1373 items per arm' was wrong IN KIND. More paraphrases of the same 75 facts add almost no information. Resolving the largest observed gap needs ~1372 EFFECTIVE observations, which at rho=0.5 means ~857 distinct facts and at rho=0.7 means ~1063 — against the 73 available. The review anticipated exactly this: DeepKnowledge reports diminishing returns past a few phrasing variants, and warns that semantic diversity must not be reduced to paraphrase volume.
CORRECTION_clustering.connects_to_the_coverage_gap: The binding constraint is the FACT POOL, not the probe count. Kanto's extraction coverage is 0.3529 against a 0.6 gate, so the domain cannot currently supply the facts this experiment needs. The coverage failure is not merely a data-quality nit — it is what makes the replay curve unresolvable on this domain at any probe-set size.
CORRECTION_clustering.fix_landed: eval_probes.summarize_hits now reports n_independent_facts and items_per_fact beside n, with a note that any cross-run comparison must use n/DEFF. The denominator can no longer be read as independent without the reader being told otherwise.
